title: Rio Branco Advances with Youth Player Deals in U-20 Cup
seoTitle: Rio Branco Advances in U-20 Cup Youth Player Negotiations
subtitle: Espírito Santo Club Retains Economic Rights Percentages in All Transfers
excerpt: During the first phase of the U-20 Copa do Brasil, Rio Branco-ES unveiled its strategy to turn its youth academy into a revenue source, negotiating ten players with.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Rio Branco-ES, Vasco's opponent in the first phase of the U-20 Copa do Brasil, gained prominence by announcing the negotiation of ten players formed or developed in its youth academy to clubs from series A, B, C, and to the international market.

Strategy for Retaining Economic Rights

The club adopted the premise of retaining percentages of economic rights in all operations, guaranteeing financial participation in future transfers should the athletes advance in their careers.

Key Deals Concluded

Among the agreements signed are the loan of Breno Melo to São Bernardo-SP, with 50% of the economic rights remaining with Rio Branco, and the definitive transfer of Rafael Gabriel to Fortaleza, with 40% retained.

  • Kauã Santos was sold to Avaí, with 40% of the economic rights retained.
  • Levi Santos was loaned to Volta Redonda until 2027, with 100% of the economic rights under Rio Branco's control.

Transfers of Promising Young Players

The club also moved athletes from the U-17, U-15, and U-13 categories, such as Miguel Ribeiro (12 years old) to Atlético-MG, Davi Uler (13 years old) to Cruzeiro, and Arthur Oliveira (15 years old) to Internacional, retaining percentages of economic rights in each case.

Expansion of Relationship Network

According to the Youth Academy CEO, former player Muriqui, the strategy expands Rio Branco's relationship network with clubs such as Fortaleza, Internacional, Atlético-MG, Cruzeiro, Atlético-GO, Avaí, and Volta Redonda, in addition to opening doors to the international market, including Italy.

Expected Financial Impact

By creating a portfolio of sports assets, Rio Branco expects that the appreciation of players throughout their careers will generate new revenues in future transfers, strengthening the institution's financial structure while continuing to develop talent.
